name: arrow-and-swipe-card-carousel
display_name: Card carousel: arrows always, swipe natively, auto-advance only if asked
description: A horizontally scrolling track of cards. Native scroll-snap does the swiping, so it works with no JavaScript at all; JavaScript adds arrow controls, keyboard stepping, and an optional auto-advance that yields to the visitor.

contract.outcome: the track scrolls to the following card AND a live region announces its position ("Card N of M") — the announcement is the outcome, not decoration
contract.evidence: behaviour.js goTo(current+1, true); live page carries one [data-hcc-live] region with aria-live

contract.outcome: as above, in reverse; wraps at the ends
ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on the carousel do exactly what the arrow controls do, with the same announcement
contract.why: a control that only responds to a pointer is not a control for everyone; keyboard equivalence is contract, not polish

contract.outcome: auto-advance stops and the control's accessible name flips to its inverse ("Start automatic rotation" ↔ "Pause automatic rotation") — the state is announced, not just drawn
contract.evidence: behaviour.js pauseBtn branch is inside `if (autoplay …)`; the LIVE page has data-hcc-autoplay="false" and ships no [data-hcc-pause] element at all — the contract observed in production

contract.outcome: a real page load of the card's own destination
contract.see: harvest/HARVEST_02 §4 — on the live page every card's destination is currently dead (bugs_open/071's class). The clause is right; the site is wrong, which is the point of declaring it.

automatic_triggers.when: the carousel scrolls out of view (IntersectionObserver, 0.25)
automatic_triggers.outcome: auto-advance suspends; it resumes on return
automatic_triggers.why: a rotation nobody can see burns battery and moves content under a returning visitor

automatic_triggers.when: the visitor hovers or focuses anything inside
automatic_triggers.outcome: auto-advance suspends until they leave — reading is never interrupted by the component moving
auto-advance never starts and scrolling is instant rather than smooth

automatic_triggers.when: the visitor swipes/scrolls the track directly
automatic_triggers.outcome: the component re-derives which card is current (120 ms after the scroll settles) so the next arrow press continues from where the visitor is, not from where the code last was

states.why: a control that cannot change anything must not be presented — the `no-inert-control` invariant, third independent sighting

degraded_states.when: the JS bundle fails to load or is blocked
degraded_states.outcome: the track still scrolls and snaps natively, every card is still a real link, and the arrows (which are the only JS-dependent part) simply do nothing visible
degraded_states.why: the behaviour is an enhancement over a working component, not the component itself
degraded_states.evidence: scroll-snap lives in the template's CSS; behaviour.js only binds controls

degraded_states.when: the behaviour script is included more than once (it ships in a site-wide bundle)
degraded_states.outcome: initialisation must be idempotent — one set of handlers, one timer
degraded_states.note: hero-card-carousel guards by scoping to its own root and re-querying; stat-band guards with an explicit flag (CC-006). Two different mechanisms for one requirement — a register clause makes it a decision rather than an accident.

prev_control.reason: Serves the 'previous' control's exists-only-when clause. Declared but not referenced by any check because no attribute assertion exists at either tier, so 'this element does/does not carry the attribute' cannot be checked. Kept so the requirement survives until the harness can run it — deleting it would delete the record of what the clause needs.

checks._unsupported: page_status_ok takes no URL (HARVEST_01 §3.3) — this is the check that would have caught four dead cards on the live page today
neither zero-count assertions nor conditional checks exist
